name: @auracheck-ai/mcp

tools.name: auracheck.read_code
tools.description: Read a text file from the developer repo. Path is relative to repo root and must fall within configured codeRoots. Use to understand routes, components, validators, and fixtures before generating a testcase.

tools.name: auracheck.list_dir
tools.description: List entries of a directory inside the developer repo. Path is relative to repo root.

tools.name: auracheck.search_code
tools.description: Search developer repo (within codeRoots) for a substring or regex. Returns up to 200 matches with file + line + preview. Use to locate routes, handlers, components by name.

tools.name: auracheck.whoami
tools.description: Report sign-in status, the base URL, and the project this MCP session is bound to, plus a nextStep hint for what to do next (sign in, bind a project, or nothing — already set up). Safe to call first, before signing in.

tools.name: auracheck.login
tools.description: Sign in to AuraCheck through the browser (same OAuth/PKCE flow as `auracheck login` in a terminal) — no terminal needed. Opens the system browser and waits up to ~90s for the person to click Allow. If it times out before that, it returns the sign-in url and 'Not finished — call auracheck.login again to resume.'; calling it again starts a fresh attempt (no duplicate tokens are saved — a new sign-in simply replaces the old one for this baseUrl). On success the token is saved exactly like the CLI command, and tool calls that needed auracheck.login now work.

tools.name: auracheck.logout
tools.description: Forget the locally saved sign-in for this baseUrl. Local only — does not revoke the token on the server (do that from Profile → Active devices if needed).

tools.name: auracheck.bind_project
tools.description: Set the default AuraCheck project for this repo (if a .sixseven/config.json binding exists or can be created in the current working directory) or, otherwise, as this machine-wide default — the same fallback project tools use when no projectId is passed. Verifies the id against auracheck.list_projects when signed in. Onboarding order: auracheck.login → auracheck.list_projects → ask the person which one → auracheck.bind_project.

tools.name: auracheck.get_screenshot
tools.description: Download a run screenshot (or any authenticated blob) to a local file and return its path, so it can then be opened and looked at. Pass a `screenshotUrl` straight from auracheck.get_evidence — those are bare paths that cannot be fetched without the bound base URL and CI token, so this is the only way to actually SEE a step's screenshot. Reach for it whenever a failure's cause is visual: 'the page froze' is often disproved by two consecutive screenshots being identical, or by the page rendering fine with a control merely disabled.

url.description: screenshotUrl from get_evidence, e.g. '/api/blob/screenshots/<runId>/<caseId>-step14.png'. An absolute URL is accepted only on the bound host.

outPath.description: Where to write it. Defaults to a temp file named after the blob.

tools.name: auracheck.account_status
tools.description: Who the signed-in user is, their role, their company's plan/trial state, days and runs left, and the projects they can reach. Call this first in every conversation.

tools.name: auracheck.list_projects
tools.description: List the AuraCheck projects this sign-in can reach (id, name, platforms, defaultConfigurationId). Pass a project id as `projectId` to any project tool to work outside the currently set project.

tools.name: auracheck.set_project
tools.description: Confirm an AuraCheck project id is reachable and set it as the project for this session. Advisory: still pass `projectId` explicitly to tools when working across more than one project in the same conversation.

tools.name: auracheck.create_project_from_url
tools.description: "Start testing my website": create a new AuraCheck project with the given URL as its web environment. Needs the manageProjectSetup permission.

tools.name: auracheck.list_features
tools.description: List features (groups of testcases) for a project. Each feature has an id and a name. Pick the most relevant feature id before creating a testcase.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.create_feature
tools.description: Create a new feature in a project. Use when no existing feature fits the testcase you are about to create.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.delete_feature
tools.description: Delete a feature. Requires manageTestCases. Without `confirm: true` this is a DRY RUN — it only shows the feature's name and how many testcases it holds; nothing is deleted on the first call. Testcases linked to a run are soft-deleted (reparented, run history kept); unlinked ones are removed permanently. Pass `cascade: true` to also remove sub-features.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.list_testcases
tools.description: List testcases for a project, optionally filtered by platform (web/android/ios). Each case carries `prelationTestCaseId` and, when set, a joined `prelationTestCase` — the setup case AuraCheck runs automatically right before it. Use this to find an existing login/setup case before creating a new one.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.get_testcase
tools.description: Fetch a single testcase by id. `steps` comes back as the Midscene YAML/JSON string the server stores, not an array — parse it before editing, and pass it back through update_testcase in either form. Also carries `prelationTestCaseId` and, when set, a joined `prelationTestCase`.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.create_testcase
tools.description:
Create a new testcase under an AuraCheck feature. `steps` is the Midscene flow: pass EITHER an array of flow items (each item one action, e.g. { aiTap: "Sign in" }, { aiInput: "user@example.com", locate: "Email field" }, { aiAssert: "Dashboard is visible" }) OR a YAML/JSON string shaped as tasks[]. Array of Midscene flow items (auto-wrapped into tasks[]), or a YAML/JSON string shaped as `tasks: [{ name, flow }]`. Recognized action keys: aiTap, aiInput, aiAssert, aiQuery, aiHover, aiWaitFor, aiKeyboardPress, aiScroll, aiAction, sleep, javascript, aiUploadFile, aiHumanInput, aiExpectDownload, mailTmInbox, mailTmWaitOtp, mailTmWaitLink, otpInbox, otpWaitOtp. A bare array is auto-wrapped. Android/iOS cases are authored here exactly like web ones; they are RUN by a person in the AuraCheck desktop app on their own device (see start_run).

PRELATION — before writing `steps`, decide whether this case needs a starting state (logged in, on a specific page, seeded data). If it does, set `prelationTestCaseId` to an existing setup case (find one with list_testcases) instead of copying its steps into every case; create the setup case first if none exists. AuraCheck runs the prelation case automatically immediately before this one every time it runs — never add the prelation case to a run yourself. A prelation must be in the same project and never points at itself or forms a cycle.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.update_testcase
tools.description: Patch an existing testcase — only the fields you pass are touched. Useful in the auto-fix loop after reading evidence from a failed run. A `steps` patch accepts the same shapes as create_testcase. `patch.prelationTestCaseId` sets/replaces the setup case AuraCheck runs automatically before this one; pass `null` to clear it. It cannot be set to the case's own id, a case from another project, or create a cycle — the server rejects those.

tools.name: auracheck.delete_testcase
tools.description: Delete 1–500 testcases. Requires manageTestCases. Without `confirm: true` this is a DRY RUN — it only lists what would be deleted and asks you to re-call with confirm:true; nothing is deleted on the first call. A case already linked to a run is soft-deleted (run history kept); a case never attached to a run is removed permanently.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.list_runs
tools.description: List recent runs for a project, optionally filtered by platform.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.create_run
tools.description: Create a new run for one or more testcases. Defaults: caseSelectionMode="select". Returns the created run object including its id. An android/ios run is created here as usual, but only a person can start it: in the AuraCheck desktop app on their device.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.execute_run
tools.description: Trigger execution of an existing WEB run. Fire-and-forget: the runner state lives in AuraCheck. Use wait_for_run to await terminal status. Android/iOS runs never execute on AuraCheck's servers: for those this returns a blocked result telling the person to open the run in the desktop app and click Run on local / Run on iOS.

tools.name: auracheck.cancel_run
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight run. Idempotent for queued runs; for inline runs the cancel may take effect at the next case boundary.

tools.name: auracheck.wait_for_run
tools.description: Poll a run until it reaches a terminal status (passed/failed/cancelled/error) or the timeout elapses. Returns the final run object plus a summary of per-case statuses. Remote caps the wait at 45s and returns `pollAgain:true` if still running — call it again (the user also gets an email when the run finishes). Local can wait up to 300s. An android/ios run stays pending until a person starts it in the AuraCheck desktop app.

tools.name: auracheck.get_run
tools.description: Fetch a single run by id including current status, started/completed timestamps, and reportUrl when available.

tools.name: auracheck.get_run_report
tools.description: Results of a run as the Run Report groups them: case counts (passed/failed/skipped/pending) plus buckets — potential bugs (with bug report, severity), script issues, blocked cases and passed cases. Read-only.

tools.name: auracheck.list_run_testcases
tools.description: List the testcases attached to a specific run.

tools.name: auracheck.get_evidence
tools.description: Aggregate evidence for a finished (or in-progress) run: per-case attempts, latest step events, failed-step screenshots and error messages, and the AuraCheck report URL. A failed step that hung also carries stallDiagnostics. Filter by caseId to narrow scope. Use after wait_for_run to diagnose failures.

tools.name: auracheck.list_schedules
tools.description: List the recurring run schedules of a project. Each schedule carries its cron expressions, IANA timezone, computed nextFireAt (UTC), platform, case filter and notify recipients.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.get_schedule
tools.description: Fetch a single schedule by id. lastFiredAt reflects CLOCK-driven fires only — run_schedule_now deliberately leaves it untouched; use list_schedule_fires for the full history.

tools.name: auracheck.create_schedule
tools.description: Create a recurring run schedule. cronExpressions is 5-field cron evaluated in `timezone` (IANA, e.g. 'Asia/Jakarta'); several expressions are allowed. caseFilter picks what runs: { mode: 'all' } for every case on the platform, or { mode: 'feature', featureIds } to narrow (get ids from list_features). notifyUserIds must come from list_schedule_recipients. Prefer enabled:false while testing, then enable once the cadence reads right.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.update_schedule
tools.description: Patch an existing schedule — pause it (enabled:false), change cadence, retarget its configuration, or edit notify recipients. Only the fields you pass are touched.

tools.name: auracheck.delete_schedule
tools.description: Delete a schedule permanently. Runs it already created are kept; only the cadence goes away. Prefer update_schedule with enabled:false to pause it instead.

tools.name: auracheck.run_schedule_now
tools.description: Fire a schedule immediately on the identical code path the clock uses — works on a paused schedule too. Returns { outcome, runId }: 'run_created' means a run was started (feed runId to wait_for_run), while 'skipped_overlap' means a previous run of this schedule is still live and 'no_cases' means the case filter matched nothing. Skips are reported, not thrown.

tools.name: auracheck.list_schedule_fires
tools.description: History of a schedule's occurrences, newest first: when it fired, the outcome, and the run it created (if any).

tools.name: auracheck.list_schedule_recipients
tools.description: The users that may be put in a schedule's notifyUserIds. Resolved exactly the way the server resolves recipients at send time.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.start_exploration
tools.description: Trigger AuraCheck's crawler on a set of seed URLs for a project. Returns a snapshot immediately (job runs in background); poll with get_exploration. One job per project at a time — calling this while a job is already running returns the live snapshot.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.get_exploration
tools.description: Return the latest exploration snapshot for a project (or null if none has ever run). Shape: { jobId, status, visited, anchorsUpserted, loggedIn, errors[] }. Use to await completion before generating testcases that depend on discovered routes/anchors.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.file_bug
tools.description: Open an issue report (bug) against a project. Use this only after the auto-fix loop has identified a real application defect (not a flaky testcase). Severity must be 'critical', 'high', 'medium', or 'low'. Pass evidence URLs (screenshotUrl from get_evidence) in evidences[].

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.list_bugs
tools.description: List issue reports (bugs) for a project. Use to check whether a defect has already been reported before filing a new one.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

tools.name: auracheck.get_bug
tools.description: Fetch a single issue report by id.

tools.name: auracheck.test_my_flow
tools.description: One-shot: turn a plain-English request ("check that sign-up works") into a test plan, show it, then run it on confirmation and summarize the result with a link. Call once without `confirm` to see the plan; call again with `confirm:true` once the person agrees to run it.

projectId.description: AuraCheck project id (see list_projects). Defaults to the project set for this session.

instructions:
This server works before sign-in: auracheck.whoami, auracheck.login, auracheck.logout, auracheck.bind_project, and tools/list all work with no credentials. Every other tool needs a sign-in and a bound project.

First-run order for a new user: 1) auracheck.whoami to check status. 2) If not signed in, auracheck.login — it opens the person's browser and waits up to ~90s for them to click Allow; if it times out, call it again. 3) auracheck.list_projects, ask the person which project, then auracheck.bind_project({ projectId }). 4) Proceed with the project tools (they fall back to the bound project when projectId is omitted).

You are connected to AuraCheck, an AI testing service that runs real browser tests on the user's website.
Start every conversation with account_status. It tells you the user's role, plan, days/runs left and their projects.
Talk in outcomes, not YAML. Many users are not engineers. Say "I'll check that new users can sign up" — not
"I'll create a Midscene flow". After a run, report: what passed, what failed in one sentence each, the likely cause,
the run link, and a screenshot for the first failure. Only show steps/YAML if the user asks.
Before writing or running any test: (1) find the project (list_projects; ask if more than one fits);
(2) PRELATION — decide whether the test needs a starting state (logged in, a specific page, seeded data). If yes,
list_testcases and reuse an existing setup case (e.g. "Login") via prelationTestCaseId. Never copy login steps into a
test. If none exists, ask the user for the test account to use, create the setup case first, then reference it.
AuraCheck runs the setup case automatically — never add it to a run yourself. (3) check list_testcases for a duplicate.
For "test this on my site" requests use test_my_flow; it shows a plan first — confirm it with the user before running.
Runs take minutes: start the run, give the link, then call wait_for_run; if it returns pollAgain, tell the user it's
still running and call it again (or come back later — they also get an email).
Never ask for or repeat passwords, PINs or OTP codes in chat. Test accounts and secrets are stored in AuraCheck
(Project → Test accounts); tell the user to add them there. Tool results never contain secret values.
Delete tools are dry-run first: show what will be deleted and get an explicit "yes" before confirm:true.
If a tool says the plan is read-only or the trial limit is reached, relay its message and next step exactly; don't retry.
Apps on localhost, an office VPN or an intranet can't be reached by AuraCheck's cloud runner: suggest the AuraCheck
desktop app or the local MCP (npx @auracheck-ai/mcp). Android/iOS runs only start from the desktop app on the user's device.

This server also runs on your machine, so it additionally offers read_code, list_dir and search_code over the developer's repo (within configured codeRoots) — use them to understand routes, components, validators and fixtures before generating a testcase. It also offers login, logout and bind_project for local sign-in and project binding; account_status/whoami work here too.
